item.title: Sharon Jarvis
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
Riding Disciplines

Para Dressage

Coach(es)

Rozzie Ryan

Horses

Lord Larmaque, Parkiarrup Edward, Applewood Odorado

Breed(s)

Hanoverian, TB, KWPN

Is your area a noted horse district?  If so give details:

I live at Brookleigh Equestrian Estate when I am in Perth. It is located in the Swan Valley and it is a very ‘horsey’ area. The family farm is in the South West of the state in Donnybrook. It is a farming district known more for it’s Apple Growing Industry.                        

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

 I require my horses to have enough energy and Power yet not become hot and fizzy and also maintain a good healthy weight.

Name the most influential person in your riding career and why:

 I have a few, my Dad, he never said I couldn’t do something, I just had to work my butt of to prove I could, my first coach Karen Spice who really introduced me to dressage, I will never forget that first feeling of half pass and piaffe. Roz Tippet who helped me believe I could do anything as good as anyone else and now Rozzie Ryan because she is simply amazing as a rider and coach.

Describe your first pony:

 A very naughty, cheeky 10.3hh Pinto Australian Pony named Arden Vale Tiny Tonka (Tonka Toy) Every time he cantered he would buck me off! And then he would be so stubborn he would only go if he was following someone!

Describe your most embarrassing (horse related) moment, if any:

Falling off in the Show Ring in a rider class, only to get back on and place 3rd, and yes there were more than 3 people in the class!!

Do you have any 'other' animals?

I have a dog named Grover who is a golden retriever and a cat called Schnappy

What are your ambitions?

To win gold for Australia at the Paralympics and to compete in open dressage at Grand Prix.

What do you require from your horse feed?

An excellent quality product made from the best ingredients that my horses love to eat and that is easy to feed. 

2010 - Winning 2 Bronze Medals at the World Equestrian Games in Kentucky.

2008 - Representing Australia at Beijing Paralympics and placing 4th

Representing WA at the EA Show Horse Nationals in the Senior Rider Class (first Para rider to do this)

Eventing at Preliminary Level and placing amongst the able bodied riders (Something I never imagined I could)

item.title: Emma Mason
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
Name:

Emma Mason

Riding Discipline:

Show jumping

What are the biggest highlights in your riding career?

Being shortlisted for the 2012 London Olympics on "F1 Pharinelli", winning Adelaide 3* on Warrego Marco Polo, and winning the inaugural Scone Ellerston 4* riding KPH Kingfisher.

Name your favourite horse(s) through your career and what makes them so special?

That's a really hard one. I've had the privilege of riding some pretty amazing horses, all so different and all special in their own right. But Warrego Marco Polo ("Marcus") and KPH Kingfisher ("Kwinky") would have to be the standouts.

What Pryde's EasiFeed products do you use and how do they help meet the needs of both you as an owner/rider and your horses?

I have been feeding Pryde's EasiRide for as long as I've been riding professionally - I love this feed as a staple, for high level competition horses right through to green youngsters and horses off the track. They do so well on it, and they love it. For those in 3DE work, I add EasiResult and EnergyPak, which keeps them feeling energetic and fresh even in heavy work.

What event on the equestrian calendar do you look forward to the most each year?

Adelaide. There is just something so unique and special about riding cross country in the middle of the city.

If you could have dinner with anyone in the world, who would it be?

My husband, Brett. But if he couldn't make it, Bradley Cooper.

Best piece of advice you have heard regarding horses?

Slower is faster.

If you could go back and tell your younger self a piece of advice, what would it be?

Work hard to achieve success but don't forget to enjoy the process, the day-to-day. And travel.

Describe your first pony

I've actually never had a pony! I was 13 when I got my first horse, and she was a 15.2h TB x QH mare named Gypsy.

item.title: John Thompson
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
Riding Discipline:

dressage / sand dancing / I do the one where the horse prances around the arena

Breed:

warmblood

Your coach(es):

The arena mirrors combined with a video camera and a very self critical nature do a pretty good job.

Name the most influential person in your riding career and why:

My mum - she’s wonderful. She got us into riding as kids and gave it up herself for us. She has always been there and has believed in and supported me my whole career. She’s come back to riding herself - now she drives 6 hours to a clinic to come have a lesson with me!.

Describe your riding history:

Lot of horses and even more circles.

Special highlight(s) in your riding career:

Being named reserve for the Rio Olympics, selected for the WEG and ranked in the top 100 riders in the world in 2016 and 2017 and currently being long listed for Tokyo Olympics

What are your ambitions?

World domination, riding a unicorn and a perhaps medal or two in between

Have you trained or coached any riders who have had success?

I have Many! My clientele ranges from amateurs to seasoned professionals - for some, success has been finding new confidence in their riding and the choices they are making in their training and for others it’s been moving up the levels and achieving their desired competition results. To me, one does not outweigh the other.

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

I’ve always found it is important to make sure your horse has a balanced diet to complement their training - as their health starts from the inside out.

Which Pryde’s feeds do you use and why do you like them?:

Most of my horses are on EasiPerformance, I find this provides them with all the energy they need to train and perform at the top of the sport, and it keeps them looking amazing too!

My young horses are fed EasiResult, its perfect for providing all the goods to keep them looking and feeling great without heating them up.

item.title: Bronwyn and James Harvey
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
James Harvey

Owner and manager at Patanga Park Performance Horses and Equine Dentistry Australia.

James started riding horses at the age of two. He started Pony Club as soon as he was aloud and by the age of ten it was apparent show jumping was his passion.

James Mum Julie was his early inspiration, carting him all over the country to shows, lessons and anything to do with the horses. Julie encouraged and supported James with all the passion of a proud mother until sadly she passed away in 2006.

Lisa Stevens has also been, and continues to be another huge support and mentor for James. Lisa started coaching James when he was 11 years old and they still speak often.

James also gives his wife Bronwyn much of the credit for his success with the horses. He says she is his greatest support and his best friend.

James has had many highlights in his show jumping career, he lists several of these as:

  • Competing in the USA under the guidance of world renown rider Margie Engle

  • High placings in many World Cup classes

  • Being the first rider in Australia to gain his MER for the 2020 Tokyo Olympics

James not only rides, breeds and produces performance horses but he is also a qualified equine dentist. Between horse shows James will treat upwards of 50 horses every week. He travels all over Australia and Tasmania looking after horses dental care, from top athletes to retired old-timers and paddock pets.

James feeds and recommends Prydes, he says he is positive the feed the horses are getting right throughout their life has everything to do with their performance and longevity. He is very proud to be a sponsored rider and to be associated with such a well-known and trusted product. James enjoys the fact; no matter where he travels to compete in Australia the Prydes logo is there, it’s a real family of like-minded horse people.

Bronwyn Harvey

Owner and manager at Australian Equine Reproduction, Yarra Valley Victoria, Australia.

I started vet nursing in 2001 at Montrose Veterinary Clinic, shortly after I began work for Dr Mike Basset and Dr Lindsay Williams at Lilydale Animal Hospital and Yarra Valley Equine Hospital.

This was a very busy equine practise employing 15 to 20 staff at a time.

I quickly worked through my studies and took on managing the equine practise and the ever-growing AI and reproduction side of the business.

Dr Lindsay Williams was one of the first vets in the area to start working with both chilled and frozen semen in horses, his background in research, genetics and general hard working ethic resulted in the clinic having extremely high pregnancy rates.

Lindsay soon became my teacher and mentor in all things AI.

In 2008 James and I bought a farm beside Dr Willams in the Yarra Valley and continued to grow the breeding side of the business.

The business continued to grow and Dr Amber Lavery joined our practice. Dr Lavery brought many excellent skills to the practise, not least managing mares that had been very difficult to get pregnant. At this time we also expanded the business into offering walk on services for Stud Book Thoroughbred mares and foaling down.

Australian Equine Reproduction has grown and adapted throughout the years, as has the industry in general.

All mares both wet and dry are fed on Prides Bio Mare.

We recommend mare owners feed their pregnant mares with Pryde’s Bio Mare throughout pregnancy with the addition of 300 Elite.

Any mares struggling to hold weight, which can occur when lactating, will be fed Pryde’s Rebuild, this has become one of my favourite feed supplements.

The Pryde’s sponsorship program allows us the support to ensure our horses and our clients horses are always getting the best. I often drop the reps a quick message with questions on what a horse should be on, case specific. The answers are always quick and to the point.

We love being associated with an organisation which is recognised Australia wide for providing the best feed horses can get.

item.title: Wyatt Young
item.dc:creator: Llama Blue
item.description:
Riding Disciplines
Camdrafting, Stock Horse Classes and Hacking
item.content:encoded:
Riding Disciplines

Campdrafting, Stock Horse Classes. I used to do a lot of Hacking and some dressage.

Coach(es)

Ross Green, Gerald Obrien, Allan Young, Troy Palmer, Mum and Dad, they have all helped and guided me through my short riding career so far.

Horses

Cedervale Moonlight, Cedervale Noire, Cedervale Jekyllin, Cedervale Twist, plus a lot more that I regularly compete on throughout the year.

Is your area a noted horse district?  If so give details:

Yes, I reside in Tamworth. Tamworth is extremely horse orientated, with a number of different disciplines happening all the time from Campdrafting, Showing, Show jumping, Cutting, Team Penning etc.

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

I always need my horses wether competition horses, young horses or broodmares, I need them in the best possible condition at all times, Prydes allows my horses to be in the best possible shape for competition as they are on an extremely good and healthy diet all of the time.              

Name the most influential person in your riding career and why:

A number of people have helped me over the years and each and every one have been influential within their own right.

Describe your first pony:

My first ponies name was "Snoopy". He was a grey gelding. He was a fabulous first pony that I thoroughly enjoyed.

Describe your riding history:

I started when I was very young, 2-3, and haven’t stopped yet, I have always rode horses, after school, within school holidays, something I have just always done and something I do not plan on giving up anytime soon.

Do you have any hobbies/interests?

Not exactly, horses are the main game

Do you have any 'other' animals?

Yes, we have around 70 horses to date, as my family have a Australian Stock horse stud named Cedervale. We also run around 400-500 head of cattle between a couple of properties.

What are your ambitions?

Not exactly sure, although I don’t see myself leaving the horse industry, whether a farrier, trainer etc.

What do you require from your horse feed?

I require my horses to be in the best possible shape whilst competing, they must have the correct energy levels whilst being in the best condition, as presentations everything, I believe Prydes is the only feed that provides everything for my horses.

Cool, responsive energy - Yes

High Energy - Yes

Energy for work, without excess calories - Yes

Coat condition - Yes

Specific young horse feeds - Yes

Which Pryde's feeds do you use and why do you like them?

Pryde's EasiResult is the main feed that I feed to my horses from breakers to competition horses. I also will feed Prydes Phase 2, to my yearlings, broodmares and stallions.

Have you trained or coached any riders who have had success?

Not to date.

How will Pryde's Sponsorship make a difference to you?

Being sponsored by Prydes, I am very proud to represent such and amazing product that I use and recommend continuously. The sponsorship will enable others to become familiar with this top quality product, which will encourage more and more people to purchase this quality product.

What do you think you can do to make a difference for Pryde's?

As I use and recommend Prydes where ever I go and to everyone, I hope that I can contribute to more and more people using the Prydes Easifeed products. I believe that because my horses are always in the best possible condition, people take notice of how well they look and go, therefore my horses will speak for themselves which will encourage more and more people to use the Prydes Easifeed range.

2012, 2013, 2014 - Highest Placed Youth Maiden Series Campdraft, Australian Stock Horse National Youth Show

2012 - ABCRA Australian Champion Juvenile Campdraft Rider

2012 - ABCRA Australian Champion, All Round Campdraft horse, won by Cedervale Jekyllin

2011 - ABCRA, Australian Reserve Champion, Juvenile Rider

2011 - Australian Stock Horse World Show, Youth Challenge Champion

2012 - Australian Stock Horse National Show, Youth Challenge Champion

item.title: Billy Raymont
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
Having begun riding at a very early age and as a result of a strong family involvement in the sport, Billy’s life has since been dedicated to producing showjumping horses to the highest level. He has represented Australia on multiple National, senior and young rider teams, and has campaigned & produced world class horses, a few of those include Royal Selections, Dutch Choice, Balmoral Tim Tram, Nicalette NZPH and Stardom. Billy won the Australian World Cup League in 2005 and was Runner up in 2010, 2011 & 2013 as well as won many state and National titles including the 2011 & 2013 New Zealand National Senior Title.

Billy is renowned for his ability in getting the best out of every horse, and every ride he gives. He believes his success is the result of his approach towards his horses, “treat them as serious horses, take your time in training and do not rush them, your horse has to be confident, confidence comes from trust and that comes from creating a partnership.” Billy is envied for his knack with young or difficult horses, which complements his belief in the importance of providing horses with the best possible start to their performance career.

What is special about Billy is his concern towards promoting showjumping in Australia, to ensure its future is progressive. He does this through aiding new and experienced riders to develop their skills and to encourage and assist those not only interested in being successful riders but also in preparing, coaching, management, and course building. His charm does not prevent his objective assessment of both horse and rider, his ability to identify strengths, make adjustments and improve each and every combination presented to him are an asset.

item.title: Ross Smith
item.dc:creator: kylieh@prydes.com.au
item.content:encoded:
Riding Disciplines

Showjumping Eventing

Horses

Quite Cassini, Doyata , Carlson 83 , Cupido Castello, Conquest , Miss Money Penny, Colorado MVNZ , Capioera , Rangeview Amigo, Romantic Dream , Balmoral Cougar Pedy.

Breed(s)

All purpose but mainly European bred and imported horses , all specifically chosen to be produced to the upper levels and sold.

Name the most influential person in your riding career and why?

Several people firstly my parents Bruce and Judy Smith , they taught me that to achieve you have to work hard and believe in what you are doing . My parents have been around horses all their lives and their knowledge and horsemanship has been so influential in what we are doing today .

Coloman De Bolgar a living legend in his day he taught me at a young age to understand the horse and train yourself to be disciplined .

Later years my wife Mel she has taught me the art of presentation of the horses and to have faith in what we do .

Describe your riding history:

We grew up riding horses before we could walk , lived in the country in North Canterbury in the South island of NZ where we had ponies and rode all through our junioryears competing at pony club level and also ESNZcompetitions , when i left school i rode hacks and competed all over NZ up to the Grand Prix level in showjumping and Advanced level in eventing . In the mid nineties i decided to go to the USA and ride and work it was there that i achieved some very goos results and rodde at some amazing venues . I won the lone Star Grand prix in Dallas Texas and was placed in several other major GP classes all over the USA , i was also extremely lucky to qualify to ride a horse at Madison Square gardens in New York which was the biggest indoor show in America

Upon returning from the USA i have based out of Australia and New Zealand doing the showjumping seasons in both countries .

In 2013 Mel and i sat down and made a family decision to base permanently in Australia , we have bought a place in conjunction with her brother Matthew and his partner Ashley in Kalbar Qld which  we are now setting up as a training establishment and also sale business .

Special highlights in your riding history:

Winning the Lone star GP in Dallas Texas

Winning the Gatton World cup in 2012 , winning the New Zealand super league series in 2011 and 2012, Danniverke World Cup and numerous other world cup pplacings , also won a large number of GP classes through out the season in New Zealand leading up to our moving to Australia

Also rode for New Zealand in the 2013 Trans tasman series .

What are your ambitions?

To run a successful business in the training and producing of top level horses .

Continue to train students to the highest level and introduce more people into this sport.

Spend as much time with my family as possible .

Have you trained or coached any riders who have had success?

We have trained a number of riders to achieve great results .

Hayley Morris represented NZ in YR classes   and has had some great wins and placings whilst here in Australiaalready, Olivia Robertson represented NZ in YR classes, Stacey Anderson 2nd in the NZ YR series, Becky Harkess 2nd in NZ pony GP at HOY , Harry Feast placed in the NZ junior YR class at HOY , Amanda Roy placed in several GP classes, Matthew Gaskeleading Qld event rider . plus a large number of students who have achieved personal best results at all levels .

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

All our horses have individual programmes and management , we have a pulse rug which is used all the time , before after and during the show season , we have a vet look at our horses on a regular basis to check that they are all fit and well .

We believe that the right combination of fee , therapeutics , and horsemanship are paramount to our business and Prydes plays a very important role in this.

item.title: Will Enzinger
item.dc:creator: Llama Blue
item.content:encoded:
Nickname

Wilski

Riding Disciplines

Eventing

Coach(es)

Charlotte Pederson, Jamie Comen

Horses

Wenlock Aquifer, Paihai Wilhelm, Bellhaven Sanskrit, Bee Bee Deeva, Equissage Dynamic Night, Stormport, Lecante, Mouse Trap.

Breed(s)

Bellhaven Stud, Thoroughbreds and Warmblood X Thoroughbred

Is your area a noted horse district? If so give details:

Yes, there are more arenas in Macclesfield than people!               

How did you come to get your horse(s):

Through owners and Breeders and organising Syndication.  

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

KISS, always think logically, and be paranoid. All horses are checked all over twice daily. Good Quality feed (Pryde's EasiFeed) and cleanliness. All equipment is washed regularly including cotton rugs (with disinfectant).                                         

Name the most influential person in your riding career:

Heath Ryan

Describe your first pony:

Black, little, naughty. Loved to buck my brother and I off regularly (we were double dinking) and then take off home. It was always a long walk.

Describe your riding history:

I started riding when I was around 7 years old. My brother and I were enrolled in a weeks holiday programme every holidays. I basically trail rode until I was 16 years old when somebody asked me if I would like to do a One Day Event. I had no idea what it was and said “yes,” of course. From there I joined pony club and moved up to Lochinvar (New South Wales), where I trained with Heath and Rozzie Ryan for three years. I really had no idea what I was doing when I first moved up there. I really owe my whole career to Heath and Rozzie, had I never trained at Lochinvar I guarantee I would not be where I am today. I learnt so much there, it was an amazing experience.

Did you belong to a Pony Club? Give details:

Yes Monbulk Pony Club, I joined when I was 16 years old. I now occasionally go back and teach when I'm available.

Do you have any hobbies/other interests?

Singing. I love it. I had lessons for a couple of years but not too recently, though I'm always happy to belt out a tune.

Describe your most embarrassing moment (horsey):

I was riding TS Jamaimo 2012 in the CCI*** class at Lakes and Craters where I was leading going into the Show Jumping phase (I was the only one left in the class).  All I had to do was jump all the jumps and go through the flags for a CCI*** win, but noooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooo!!!!!!!!!! I proceeded to go in and jump the wrong track and Eliminating myself.  That was a long truck drive home and one of the hardest Phone Calls I’ve had to make when calling the owners!

Do you have any superstitions?

I will not wear brand new breaches Cross Country. They have to of been worn at least once in the dressage phase. Though not at the same competition. If the pair are new to that competition then I can't wear them Cross Country until the next competition.

Do you have any 'other' animals?

Emily and I have 1 dog, though it looks more like a rat in a dog suit, tough I have to say I’m pretty pathetic with him!

What are your ambitions?

I want to represent Australia in eventing at the Olympic Games. That is my dream.

Which Pryde's feeds do you use and why do you like them?      

EasiResult – it is an allround feed that has a little extra in it for horses that are in work and need a little extra energy without the fizz.

Easi Response - this feed is used for nearly all of our horses and used in conjunction with Easi Result. It gives the he horses a full balanced feed which is not heating and it definitely adds weight. There is not one horse that I have feed it to that has not been neighing for more. They LOVE it!

EasiPerformance- This is added with EasiResult to give my eventers a lot more energy when they are heading for their final 6 weeks in preparation for major events like Melbourne, Adelaide and Sydney three day events.

EasiBreed- All my brood mares and young stock live on this with Lucerne chaff and they look a million bucks.

EasiOil- The breeding side and competition side are all on the omega 3,6 and 9 oil.

EasiFeed 300 Pellets - I'm using the 300 pellet to give my horses the added supplements they would lack from the pasture.

Rebuild – This has been so valuable to us over the past couple of years.  This has helped those horses struggling to bloom, these horses needing just a little more help to produce good solid muscle and topline.  It does take a little while to see the results, but when you see it it’s incredible.

Easi Sport – We have 2 horses on this feed and they have previously tied – up, since swapping to this feed we have never looked back!

Do you have any other businesses:

Emily and I own and Run Wilky Park Performance Horses.  This facility is a competition training facility where we coach riders, take horses in for training, Offer Working Pupil Positions, we also travel for clinics Australia wide and also overseas.  We have had a relationship with coaching in Japan for over 6 years now.

Special highlights in your riding career

Competing for Australia on the Australian team on the Trans Tasmin in Taupo (New Zealand) 2003. Competing at Adelaide CCI**** three years in a row finishing in the top ten each year.

Nickname

Riding Disciplines

Dressage

Horses

PPH Zeppelin, DP Weltmiesser, Larenso, Good As Gold, Longvue Florencio, Daytona, Che De Jeu, Aber Hallo 29, Furstin Friendship

Breed(s)

Warmbloods, warmblood/thoroughbred

How did you come to get your horse(s):

DP Weltmieser (Rabbit) is owned by Susie and Richard Duddy, Brian and Barbara Marheine.  Bred by Susie, he is by Weltmeyer out of an imported mare.

PPH Zeppelin (Led) was bought in Holland as an unbroken 4 yr old.  I broke him in and brought him home, then sold a half share to our great friend Helen Batson.

Good As Gold (Will) was found when Carolyn Lieutenant asked for us to find her an Australian bred horse that could fit in behind Victory Salute and carry on his legacy of promoting Australian bred horses.  He was acquired from Glen Pearce and is owned in half share between us and Carolyn. 

Che De Jeu was purchased from Holland from the stables of Edward Gal and Nicole Werner.  Previously owned by Emmy de Jeu and represented Holland in the 2013 young horse world championships in Verden.  He is owned by Howard, Sally and Steph McDonald.

Daytona Joy (DJ) is an imported mare owned by Susie Clapton of Wyandah Sport Horses.  She is by Johnson out of a Dormello/Feinerstern mare.   

Longvue Florencio (Ben) is imported from Germany by Glenn Fryer of Melbourne.  Glenn has been an Australian Representative and is a very respected Australian rider internationally.  Ben is by Florestan and has a big talent for Grand Prix. 

Larenso, Aber Hallo 29 and Furstin Friendship are all owned by Greg, Julie and Jane Farrell of Mulawa Arabian Stud.  These three horses have been imported from Europe and are based in Sydney at Mulawa.

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

Our horses care and management is our highest priority, we have a very detailed management system that caters for all our horses on an individual basis.  We ice their legs after each work session, we feed Prydes range of feeds, we feed all our additives in a specifically formulated pellet, all horses get turned out to a grass paddock daily, their legs are stable wrapped each night, they have a weekly hack out, we do night hay and check at 9pm each night, our grooms work consistently with their allocated horses so they know them inside and out and can pick up anything unusual straight away, temperatures are taken daily, they receive regular time with our Equilibrium massage pad, the list goes on…

Name the most influential person in your riding career:

Edward Gal

Special highlight(s) in your riding career:

World  Equestrian Games in Kentucky,15th in the Grand Prix and  9th in both the Grand Prix Kur and Grand Prix Special.

Describe your first pony:

Tiny Tim……he was a shocker

Describe your riding history:

Showing until age 13, polocrosse until age 16, rodeo until age 28, dressage until now

Did you belong to a Pony Club?

North Dorrigo

Do you have any hobbies/other interests?

Property development, snow skiing, love to support the Wallabies in Rugby

Describe your most embarrassing moment:

Falling off in the cut out yard at the Copmanhurst Campdraft day

Do you have any superstitions?

Yes…..not being prepared enough

Do you have any 'other' animals?

Bella my dog

What are your ambitions?

To try and produce all the quality horses I have to Grand Prix.  To do this in the best way possible so that when they get to Grand Prix they are ready for International competition.

What do you require from your horse feed?

Cool, responsive energy, High energy, Balanced minerals and vitamins, Energy for work without excess calories, Coat and muscle condition.

Which Pryde's feeds do you use and why do you like them?

EasiFibre is our main feed, we also include EasiResult, EasiResponse, Energy Pak, Prydes Oil and Polished depending on each horses’ needs. They are easy to feed and the horses really like them. Now that we have worked out the diet, my horses offer even energy levels for longer periods, which is essential for training dressage horses

Have you tried any other Pryde's Feed?

We have also  fed EasiSport and EasiPerformance in the past for certain horses needs.

Do you have any other businesses:

Property consultancy business

Have you trained or coached any riders who have had success?

Katherine Farrell, Dave McKinnon, Robbie Soster, Shane Rose, Tor Van Den Berge, Penny Castles, Anjanette Harten. I train many riders in all states that have won their respective State Championships.

How will Pryde's Sponsorship make a difference to you?

It enables me to feed the absolute best of the Prydes range.

item.title: Leanne Caban
item.dc:creator: Llama Blue
item.description:
Riding Disciplines
Rodeo - Barrel Racing and Breakaway Roping
item.content:encoded:
Riding Disciplines

Barrel Racing and Breakaway Roping

Horses

Morns Music Bar (Decker), Hootchy Kootchy Wood (Deisel) Morns Akka Dakka Roc - Barrel Racing Horses, Traditional Cutter (Gattling) - Breakaway Roping Horse

Breed(s)

Quarter Horses, a number of our horses carry the famous "Morn Deck" bloodlines. We have recently bred successfully to an imported barrel racing sire owned by Bek Knudsen of Taroom by the name of ‘Mojo’s Workin’. He carries the famous American bloodline of ‘Dash Ta Fame’.

Is your area a noted horse district?  If so give details:

Yes, some of the best rodeo competitors in the country live in Emerald.  For example 14times Australian All Round Champion Shane Kenny, Former Team Roping champions Grant Hanrahan and Brodie Moss.  Former Australian Barrel Racing and All Round Champion Bridget Brandenburg resides in Capella North of Emerald.

Special care and management considerations of your horse(s):

Conditioning through work and nutrition. Regular dental and massage care also play an important part. My husband Dale takes great care of their feet.

Name the most influential person in your riding career and why:

There have been a number of people that have had a huge impact on my chosen events. A good friend and former Australian Barrel Racing Champion and Record holder Bridget Brandenburg has helped me tremendously over the years.  There is also a great horseman by the name of Ray McGhee from whom I have gained valuable horsemanship knowledge and he fortunately lives in my home town of Emerald.   A couple of my other horsemanship idols are Ian Francis and Clinton Anderson.

Special highlight(s) in your riding career:

Breaking the Australian Barrel Racing record in 1994 and holding that for a period of 6 years.  I achieved this at the famous Mt Isa Rodeo aboard my great old horse ‘Wollombi Fabian” aka Trash.

Winning both the Australian Barrel Racing and Breakaway Roping Championships in 1995 for the Womens Professional Rodeo Association.

Being invited to travel to a Barrel Racing Farm in Qingdao, China in May 2014 to train barrel racing horses and their riders.

Having the chance to compete in a Cutting Event in Capella Qld in July 2014 on a very good mare called ‘Peptos Bonita Two’ owned by Kristine Holmes of Emerald. 

Describe your first pony:

My first pony was approximately 12hh and Grey. She was purchased as a 3 year old when I was about 6 years old and we were as green as each other. I called her Jeanie.

Describe your riding history:

I was introduced to horses by my Mum and Dad.  Mum always wanted them as a child however she didn’t have the opportunity until she met my father.  Dad trained a few racehorses when I was younger and I would ride track work for him.

I grew up doing Pony Club, then some Campdrafting and finally got hooked on Rodeo with the sport of Barrel Racing and Breakaway Roping.

Do you have any hobbies/interests?

The majority of my time is taken up with the day to day business of taking care of the horses, the home and raising my children.  I am also interested in breaking and training our young horses and getting them ready for their futurity years.

Describe your most embarrassing (horse related) moment, if any:

Using my kids as an excuse for being distracted, I neglected to put the tailgate up on my horsefloat and drove about 5km along the highway.

Do you have any 'other' animals?

We have a number of cattle that we breed for both beef and roping.  We also have 2 dogs and 2 cats and of course the chooks.

What are your ambitions?

To be competitve at a national level for as long as possible and to help evolutionise the sport of Barrel Racing in Australia.

What do you require from your horse feed?

Cool, responsive energy - for the young upcoming futurity horses

High energy - for my rodeo competition horses

Balanced minerals and vitamins - yes

Energy for work, without excess calories - yes

Coat condition - yes

No fuss breeding feeds - yes

Specific young horse feeds - in foundation stage

Which Pryde's feeds do you use and why do you like them?

I use EasiPerformance and EasiResult for my rodeo competition horses.  These feeds are very palatable and the horses perform very well on them.   I have also started to add EasiPrep Concentrate when we have a larger workload for these horses to promote their topline and muscle conditioning.

I use EasiRide for all my young colts that are in work and EasiBioMare for my broodmares.

Have you trained or coached any riders who have had success?

I have a number of clinics throughout the year and I also hold private lessons during the week for a number of young riders.  Some of these students have gone on to win buckles and titles.  After my time training riders at a Barrel Racing stable in China they have reported a number of wins to me.

How will Pryde's Sponsorship make a difference to you?

It will help raise my profile in the equine industry and keep my equine partners in the best possible shape.

What do you think you can do to make a difference for Pryde's?

With my involvement in the Rodeo and Barrel Horse industries I see my commitment to Pryde's being a very worthwhile promotional avenue for the company.
